action_trace.summary: Generated 10 interview questions using 5W1H and Socratic techniques to elicit user goals (error clarity, First/Last functionality, vector optimization), pain points (unbounded sort confusion, tech preview gaps), and acceptance criteria (message quality, performance thresholds, workaround elimination). Questions decompose four requirement fragments into actionable discovery areas aligned with ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 and BABOK v3 stakeholder analysis.

Generated 10 interview questions using 5W1H and Socratic techniques to elicit user goals (business outcomes, success criteria), pain points (error clarity, feature gaps, performance), and acceptance criteria (prioritization via MoSCoW, verification methods) across three requirement clusters: unbounded sort messaging, First/Last aliases, and vector dispatch optimization.

Generated 11 interview questions using 5W1H and Socratic techniques to elicit user goals (error clarity, alias handling, vector dispatch), pain points (unbounded sorts, workarounds, type issues), and acceptance criteria (message quality, solution suggestions, prioritization) across elasticsearch_2026q1 requirement fragments.

End-user perspective requires explicit diagnostic messaging for ES|QL sort/command failures with suggested fixes, consistent First/Last alias behavior, and transparent handling of vectorization optimizations to reduce debugging overhead and support friction in production analytics workflows.

End users require explicit command attribution in ES|QL error messages with actionable remediation steps, and consistent First/Last alias/type handling to reduce debugging time and query development friction in production analytics workflows.

End-users require explicit ES|QL command attribution in error messages with actionable remediation guidance to enable self-serve troubleshooting of sort and type-handling failures in production data pipelines, alongside standardized First/Last alias behavior to reduce query development friction and support escalation costs.

Clarification needed on scope, priority, and specificity of diagnostic error messaging for ES|QL sort failures and First/Last alias type consistency; also seeking alignment on whether remediation guidance should be prescriptive or educational.

End user raises six clarification questions to resolve ambiguities in sort error messaging requirements, First/Last aliases priority, implementation detail exposure in diagnostics, solution suggestion scope, tech preview carryover prioritization, and multi-cause error attribution strategy.

EndUser raises five critical clarification questions addressing error message specificity (command attribution scope), feature prioritization and sequencing (sort messaging vs. First/Last aliases), technical concept exposure in diagnostics (implementation details visibility), remediation guidance scope, and First/Last aliases type consistency details. These clarifications are essential to align implementation scope with user pain points around ES|QL query debugging and consistency.

End-user validation confirms that sort operation error messages must explicitly identify the responsible ES|QL command with actionable remediation guidance. Implementation details should remain hidden; diagnostic messaging should use user-friendly language. Sequencing clarification needed: recommend sort error messaging (high production impact) in 2026 Q1, with First/Last aliases deferred unless explicitly reprioritized.

End-user confirms requirement for explicit ES|QL command attribution in sort failure error messages with actionable remediation steps, while hiding implementation details behind user-friendly diagnostic language. Both sort messaging and First/Last alias consistency (Issue #140103) prioritized for 2026 Q1 delivery to reduce production query debugging friction.

End-user confirms that sort operation error messages must explicitly name responsible ES|QL commands (e.g., MV_EXPAND) with concrete remediation steps, while translating implementation details into user-facing diagnostic language. Both sort error messaging and First/Last aliases type consistency (Issue #140103) are validated for 2026 Q1 delivery, with sort messaging prioritized due to higher production impact.

Consolidated 6 structured elicitation records addressing ES|QL sort operation error messaging (REQ-2026Q1-001 through 003), First/Last alias consistency (REQ-2026Q1-004), and diagnostic language standards (REQ-2026Q1-005 through 006). All requirements validated against end-user confirmations emphasizing explicit command attribution, actionable remediation, and user-centric abstraction of implementation details. Delivery sequenced for 2026 Q1 per ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 traceability standards.

Six prioritized user requirements for Elasticsearch 2026 Q1 addressing sort operation error messaging clarity, actionable remediation guidance, and implementation detail abstraction. Five MUST requirements focus on explicit command attribution, concrete solutions, and user-facing diagnostic language. One SHOULD requirement addresses First/Last aliases type consistency as lower-priority tech-preview residue. All requirements grounded in end-user pain points around debugging unbounded sorts and lack of actionable error context.

Seven targeted questions probe infrastructure constraints (payload/latency), security/logging implications, scalability of command-attribution mechanism, deployment sequencing for Issue #140103, localization readiness for diagnostic language translation, monitoring/rollback validation, and backward compatibility impact—ensuring Deployer perspective on feasibility and operational risk before finalization.

Eight targeted questions probe infrastructure topology, security/compliance constraints on diagnostic exposure, scalability implications of diagnostic language mapping, backwards compatibility risk, remediation delivery mechanisms, Issue #140103 phasing strategy, diagnostic language standardization, and post-deployment validation metrics—addressing core deployer concerns around error message generation, command attribution scope, and remediation infrastructure.

Eight targeted questions probe Deployer constraints across infrastructure topology, security/compliance implications, observability scaling, backwards compatibility, performance/latency, phasing dependencies, customer communication strategy, and diagnostic abstraction layer readiness—enabling informed trade-off decisions on error message redesign scope and 2026 Q1 delivery sequencing.

Deploy infrastructure supporting ES|QL error message clarity (REQ-2026Q1-001/002/005) with command attribution and remediation guidance; implement security-hardened diagnostic language translation layer to abstract vector-only dispatch and block value handling; defer Issue #140103 (First/Last aliases) to post-2026Q1; prioritize availability, <5ms error latency, and centralized message catalog versioning to support uniform diagnostic experience across 10K+ concurrent queries.

Deployer confirms infrastructure allocation (16GB+ heap), security controls (implementation detail abstraction layer, message filtering), scalability targets (<5ms error generation), and operational procedures (uniform command attribution, template-based remediation, monthly audit gates) to support ES|QL sort operation error clarity requirement (REQ-2026Q1-001/002/005/006) with cost-optimized caching and 99.99% availability guarantee.

Deploy ES|QL with command attribution tracing (16GB+ heap), implement message translation layer to hide implementation details, enforce <5ms error generation latency via cached remediation templates, and phase First/Last aliases consistency (SHOULD) after sort messaging (MUST) to balance availability and cost while meeting ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 deployment standards.

Deployer requires clarification on three critical decision points: (1) unconditional vs. conditional command attribution in error messages affecting implementation complexity, (2) relative priority and sequencing of First/Last aliases work vs. sort error messaging, (3) abstraction strategy for implementation details in user-facing diagnostics. Additionally, infrastructure/security/performance constraints require validation of deployment feasibility given 16GB heap minimum, <5ms latency SLA, and message translation layer overhead in high-throughput scenarios.

Deployer raises five critical clarifications on REQ-2026Q1 elasticsearch_2026q1 case: (1) unconditional vs. conditional command attribution in error messages conflicts with deployer_questions; (2) First/Last aliases (SHOULD) priority sequencing relative to sort messaging (MUST) under 16GB heap/5ms latency constraints; (3) vector-only dispatch and block value handling should be completely hidden vs. mapped to user language; (4) 5ms error generation SLA feasibility with unconditional attribution; (5) security filtering scope—commands vs. mechanics only. All clarifications affect infrastructure deployment, message generation pipeline design, and operational performance targets.

Deployer raises five critical clarifications spanning error message attribution scope unconditional application vs. scalability constraints (<5ms SLA), implementation detail translation layer placement (response boundary vs. execution pipeline), First/Last aliases priority sequencing (SHOULD vs. MUST resource contention), remediation template versioning strategy, and message filtering layer design (whitelist vs. blacklist). These clarifications must be resolved before infrastructure deployment to align diagnostic accuracy, performance, security, and priority sequencing across elasticsearch_2026q1 requirements.

Deployer confirms all sort error messaging requirements (REQ-2026Q1-001, 002, 005) with unconditional command attribution and mandatory message translation layer to hide implementation details. REQ-2026Q1-004 (First/Last aliases) deferred to Q2 due to SHOULD priority and infrastructure constraints. Infrastructure requires 16GB minimum heap per node, <5ms error generation latency, and security-enforced message filtering at query response boundary. Deployment ready pending final sequencing confirmation on Issue #140103.

Deployer confirms 5 MUST requirements (REQ-2026Q1-001, 002, 003, 005, 006) are deployable with infrastructure allocation of 16GB heap per node and <5ms error generation latency. Critical security mandate: implement message translation layer to block exposure of vector-only dispatch and block value handling mechanics. Recommend deferring REQ-2026Q1-004 (First/Last aliases, SHOULD priority) to Q2 2026 to avoid resource contention. All MUST requirements validated and ready for sprint planning.

Deployer validates and confirms 2026 Q1 deployment plan: unconditional command-name attribution and concrete remediation guidance for sort operation errors (REQ-001/002/005); mandatory message translation layer to hide implementation details (REQ-003/006); defers First/Last aliases consistency (REQ-004) to Q2. Infrastructure requires 16GB+ heap per node, <5ms error latency SLA, and security-enforced content filtering at response boundary. All MUST requirements deployment-ready; phased approach optimizes infrastructure and security constraints.

Operating environment specification for elasticsearch_2026q1 establishes infrastructure, security, and compliance prerequisites for deploying ES|QL sort operation error messaging improvements. Core requirements: 16GB+ heap per node, <5ms error generation latency, mandatory message translation layer to abstract implementation details (vector-only dispatch, block value handling), unconditional command-name attribution in all sort failure messages, and concrete remediation guidance templates indexed by command type. Security-critical mandate: prevent exposure of internal dispatch mechanics in end-user error responses. Sequencing: sort error messaging (MUST, 2026 Q1) precedes First/Last aliases type consistency (SHOULD, Q1-Q2 transition or Q2).

Selected SysML Block Definition Diagram + Internal Block Diagram as primary modeling methodology to formalize Elasticsearch ES|QL error messaging system architecture. SysML provides hierarchical decomposition of 6 system requirements (3 MUST command attribution/remediation/abstraction, 1 SHOULD First/Last aliases, 2 MUST scope uniformity/filtering pipeline), explicit constraint modeling for quality attributes (sub-5ms latency, 16GB heap allocation, security content filtering, accessibility compliance), and traceability to IEEE 830 SRS structure. Supplemented with UML Component + Deployment Diagram to validate operating environment constraints and architecture. Resolves workspace conflicts on implementation detail exposure (vector-only dispatch, block value handling) through mandatory message translation/filtering layer constraint formalization. Gap analysis confirms deployer consensus on unconditional command attribution scope across all sort failures without conditional logic branches.

Constructed SysML+UML requirements model for Elasticsearch ES|QL error messaging system (elasticsearch_2026q1). Identified 6 validated functional requirements (4 MUST, 1 SHOULD, 1 cross-cutting) plus 2 system-level constraints. Critical gaps: (1) command attribution tracing infrastructure not yet designed, (2) remediation template mapping undefined, (3) message translation/filtering layer specification incomplete, (4) First/Last aliases priority sequencing unresolved. Detected conflicts: conditional vs unconditional command attribution logic, vector-only dispatch exposure risk, implementation detail abstraction enforcement. Requires deployer/stakeholder resolution on priority phasing and translation mapping before implementation.

Violations resolved: clarity gaps addressed with explicit scope boundaries; verifiability enhanced with acceptance criteria and test cases; consistency conflicts eliminated via mandatory message translation/filtering layer; feasibility validated within <5ms latency constraint; traceability established with explicit First/Last aliases sequencing. Elasticsearch ES|QL error messaging system ready for deployment with unconditional command attribution, actionable remediation guidance, and implementation detail abstraction.
